A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BitMark research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-quality, watermark-robustness, timing, radioactivity, and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds watermark-baseline comparisons, mixed-data radioactivity, rotation correction, additional model evaluations, and cross-dataset false-positive measurements.

M1.justification: The core bit-pattern logit bias and z-score detector remain unchanged. v2 adds single-scale embedding and detection procedures without multiscale residual processing (Algorithms 3–4), and introduces noise before encoding for BiGR detection (Appendix G). These are limited procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: MS-COCO and ImageNet coverage is retained. v2 adds LAION POP for false-positive evaluation (Table 19), horizontal and vertical flipping, and combined rotation-plus-center-crop inputs, modestly extending the existing image-watermarking scenarios.

E2.justification: v1 reports BitMark's robustness without direct numerical comparisons against other watermarking methods. v2 evaluates RivaGAN, StegaStamp, and TrustMark on Infinity-2B images alongside BitMark in Table 2, substantially expanding the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Infinity-8B and Instella configurations with delta=1.5, and BiGR configurations at two resolutions with delta=3 and 5,000 prompts. New protocols vary watermarked fine-tuning fractions, apply rotation correction with optional 50% center cropping, and transfer an MS-COCO-calibrated threshold across datasets. The original fine-tuning hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test radioactivity under clean/watermarked training mixtures (Table 6), rotation correction with and without cropping (Tables 13–14), and false-positive calibration across datasets (Table 19). Existing bit-sequence, scale, watermark-strength, and Bit-Flipper analyses are retained under reorganized appendices.

E5.justification: v2 adds a one-tailed Mann–Whitney U test and p-value reporting for the radioactivity dilution experiment (Section 4.3, Table 6). Existing mean/standard-deviation reporting continues; neither version specifies repeated-training run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover baselines, additional models, and supplementary analyses. Examples include 22.7% TPR at 1% FPR after fine-tuning with 10% watermarked data, and newly measured rotation-correction TPRs of 18.4% without correction versus 98.3% with correction. Table 5 also changes Infinity-2B radioactivity from 99.7% to 100.0%, although v2's prose still says 99.7%.

T1.justification: The bit-bias equation, z-score definition and null model, and green/red-list combinatorial reasoning are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new significance test is an empirical statistical procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution broaden the Infinity-focused scope to bitwise image generators, explicitly including Instella. The conclusion additionally claims a significant radioactivity-induced distributional shift with only 5% watermarked training data, substantially extending the stated applicability conditions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking Instella/BiGR robustness limitations to their smaller token counts, hypothesizes that Infinity-8B's lower bias reduces robustness, and interprets weak radioactivity through distribution-level significance. Existing rotation, image-quality, and large-scale false-positive limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a BitMark repository link, single-scale pseudocode, baseline message lengths, and generation settings for the added models. Existing hardware and fine-tuning details remain. Some specificity is lost from the interpolation and convolution descriptions, while BiGR's added preprocessing noise is not quantified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Instella, BiGR, TrustMark, StegaStamp, and RivaGAN, with corresponding model background and comparison positioning. The underlying discussion of LLM watermarking, diffusion watermarking, and model collapse is largely retained.

P1.justification: The appendices are extensively reorganized: limitations and related work move forward, natural-image evaluation becomes an experimental subsection, and attack material is consolidated. The title and framing are revised, and a NeurIPS checklist is appended, although much existing prose remains.

P2.justification: v2 introduces a main comparison table with baseline/model rows and flipping columns, adds several experimental tables, and relocates the original watermark-strength table to the appendix. Existing figures are resized or repositioned, and the timing table is transposed. The original qualitative image content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps in v1 through direct watermark-baseline comparisons and mixed-data radioactivity controls. Measured rotation correction and explicit model-specific weaknesses further strengthen evidence about practical applicability. These gains outweigh the new Table 5 table/prose inconsistency and incomplete specification of BiGR's noise preprocessing.
